title_en: I Cannot Do It in Chinese

sentences.en: My older sister is going to make a birthday cake and asks me to go help her.

t: cannot; do not know how to
cannot; do not know how to
sentences.en: I say: "Sorry, I don't know how to make cakes, and I don't know how to cook either."

t: cannot; do not know how to
sentences.en: My sister says: "It's fine if you don't know how — but you can't just sit there, come with me to the supermarket to buy things."
When we get to the supermarket, we buy eggs, milk, and some fruit.
After we get home, my sister makes the cake while I watch beside her, and I learn to do a little of it too.
In the evening, we eat the cake we made together.

vocab: cannot; do not know how to

quiz.q: Why does the narrator apologize at the start?
a: Doesn't know how to bake or cook

quiz.q: What does the sister say the narrator must do instead of just sitting?
a: Go to the supermarket with her

quiz.q: What do they do in the end?
a: Eat the cake they made together

grammar.p: 不会（don't know how — no learned skill）
grammar.e: 不会 + verb says you never learned how to do something, like baking or cooking.
grammar.x: 我不会做蛋糕，也不会做菜。— I don't know how to make cakes, and I don't know how to cook either.

grammar.p: 不能（cannot — not able to, due to circumstance）
grammar.e: 不能 is different from 不会: it says you're not able to do something right now, not that you lack the skill.
grammar.x: 你不能只坐着。— You can't just sit there.

grammar.e: 也 links a second negative statement to the first, showing another thing that also isn't the case.
grammar.x: 我不会做蛋糕，也不会做菜。— I don't know how to make cakes, and I don't know how to cook either.
